newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - July 2.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - July 2.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends ***********************************************
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

FRANKFURT - GWA and GfK launch a new system for measuring advertising effectiveness. GfK says it examined 17 established consumer brands over two years and measured the effectiveness of 6,000 ads to devise the new system. (Reuter)
BONN - Deutsche Telekom's Internet service, T-Online, wants to begin offering advertising on its navigation page. T-Online has 1.6 million subscribers. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - DDB chief executive Klaus Flettner is planning to leave the Duesseldorf advertising agency group just six months after assuming the top position. He is apparently leaving after losing a power struggle with creative director Paul Steenjes. (Horizont)

FRANKFURT - Aero Lloyd is to become the first German airline to make its aircraft exteriors available for advertising. The first Aero Lloyd jets to carry advertising will sport the slogan of a maker of T-shirts and tennis clothing based in Burladinger, Trigema. The company is paying a six-digit mark ($3.43) fee for each aircraft bearing its slogan. (Horizont)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

BONN - German phone giant Deutsche Telekom AG says it has reached an agreement with Bavarian medial mogul Leo Kirch and the CLT/Ufa broadcasting group to launch digital television in Germany. The three companies will hold equal stakes in Beta Research GmbH, the Kirch Group unit that developed the basic digital decoder technology, and will use Kirch's "d-box" decoder. (Reuter)
GUETERSLOH - German newspaper group WAZ will take a stake in media group CLT/Ufa, the two companies say.
(Reuter).

MUNICH - Private network Pro-7 says its market share in June rose slightly to 9.6 percent. Based on figures compiled by GfK, Pro-7 says its subsidiary Kabel 1 maintained a stable market share of four percent. Market leader RTL saw its share fall 1.1 percentage points to 15.9 percent. (Reuter)

BONN - German Post and Telecommunications Minister Wolfgang Boetsch says a decision forcing Deutsche Telekom to grant rivals access to its networks is intended to promote competition and set a tough standard. Boetsch ordered Deutsche Telekom to provide rivals with an offer for so-called unbundled interconnection by July 14. (Reuter)

NUREMBERG - Eurowings Luftverkehrs AG airline says it posted record pretax profits in 1996 of 13.7 million marks, up from 5.1 million marks in 1995. Turnover rose to 457 million marks from 410 million marks. The company says it expects turnover to rise further this year, but sees slightly lower profits due to tough competition. (Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:
WALLDORF - Thomas Holtrop is named as a member of the managing board for Bank 24. He will be in charge of marketing, electronic media and media relations. (Kress)
WALLDORF - Hartwig Conzelmann, 53, is named managing board chairman of Photo Porst AG. (Kress)

FRANKFURT - Gerrit Klein is named head of technical magazines at publishing company Deutsche Verlag. Klein, 35, will be responsible for magazines covering textiles, paper, and packing as well as the magazine Ensorga. (Reuter)
